## What we did this morning

1. We finalized a winner-copy map for all 25 connected channels: for Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Threads, SEO, GEO, note, and Substack, we recorded the winner to copy, the winner's numbers, and the strategy elements to copy.
2. We published 10 Instagram posts today: 3 in the morning frame plus 7 in the 10:27 frame.
3. We decided to switch Postiz ($51/month, 25 channels connected) to a free alternative, to cut costs and raise gross profit.

## The winner format we copy

This article copies the note winner format: a daily log with real numbers and the exact work done. The reference winner article is a daily AI side-business log that disclosed 273 followers on day 10: https://note.com/aifukugyo24/n/n12da7364bb5f . The point of the format is to hide no number, list the work concretely, and keep failures in the same article. It is the same shape as the monthly-numbers public format used by Marc Lou.

## Failures, kept in the same article

- Substack is still blocked for our agent email. On 2026-11-04 we re-tested a different entry (the onboarding sign-up dialog) and a single retry after waiting, and the same error appeared at the email step: "Something went wrong." No Substack magic link or confirmation email arrived in our agent inbox. This self-media version is the alternative publication for the same theme, because Substack itself could not be opened.
- Our Instagram accounts are still below 3 posts per account per day. The remaining slots go to the evening frame, with different themes, not reposts of the same titles.
- Our note articles did not rank in web search this morning. Tags and series grouping are the fix.

## Next steps

1. Confirm the 2 queued TikTok posts and their first views and likes.
2. Fill the remaining Instagram slots in the evening frame.
3. Work out the free Postiz replacement without dropping any of the 25 connections.
4. Publish the same format again tomorrow. On a day when numbers do not move, the article will say so, with numbers.
